For every 2<=m<=n each Hom(K_m,K_n) cell is an m-tuple of disjoint nonempty color blocks; a cell fixed under g uses q whole color cycles, with signed Lefschetz weight (-1)^(q-m). Inclusion-exclusion over onto assignments gives L(g)=sum_{j=0}^m (-1)^j binom(m,j)(1-j)^{c(g)}. Combining the known Babson-Kozlov homology wedge in degree n-m, subtracting the trivial H0 Lefschetz contribution and sign(g)=(-1)^{n-c} yields the claimed class function (all n=m boundaries included). F_{n,q} colorings with q<m<=n stabilize a repeated pair transposition, hence have zero sign-isotypic part, proving the quotient has vanishing reduced rational homology via equivariant simplicial subdivision and rational averaging. For m=3 decompose the 2^{c(g)} all-subsets module by Young rule; coefficients n-2 and n-2j+1 are nonnegative. Independently enumerated complete fixed-cell signs for (2,4),(3,4),(3,5),(4,5), 24/24/120/120 target permutations respectively; all match. Infinite claim is the counting proof plus prior nonequivariant topology.
